A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRE-RNN work. All 23 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection allow figures, tables, equations, and relocated content to be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST experiments, including accuracy, training time, convergence dynamics, feedback-scaling studies, and residual-connection comparisons.

after.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including retained results and additional topology, gradient-similarity, frozen-layer, numerical-precision, and noise-robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The core feedback-regulation and residual-connection method remains. Algorithm S2 corrects the specified convolutional clamped-phase recurrence to use clamped states, whereas v1 prints free-phase states in those updates. This is a limited algorithmic correction; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: MNIST is retained, but Fashion-MNIST evaluation is removed and CIFAR-10 natural-image classification is added. Appendix C.6 also introduces noisy-weight and noisy-state training/testing scenarios, substantially extending the evaluated environmental conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds BP with tanh and Adam to the two-hidden-layer comparison; v1 compares only P-EP and Ours there. The broader comparator families remain P-EP, BP, and FA.

E3.justification: v2 revises the alpha/beta sweep grid, adds 20-layer and additional convolutional configurations, and introduces gradient comparisons with float32/float64 and distinct noise-training/testing protocols. The stated convolutional nudging default becomes 0.25 rather than v1's general 0.1. These are reported settings and added protocols, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained dynamics and gradient-flow analyses, v2 adds before/after-training spectral-radius and convergence comparisons (Figure 5), an AGT connection-probability sweep (Figure S8), BP gradient/state alignment and precision tests (S10), frozen-layer controls (S11), and noise-robustness analyses (S12–S13). These directly investigate mechanisms and failure conditions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting remains for the main comparisons, but v2 omits the training-accuracy standard deviations reported in v1 Tables 1–2 while retaining test deviations. The newly added Figure S13 is explicitly described as a single experiment; other new analyses report five repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 replaces Fashion-MNIST scores with CIFAR-10 results and adds deeper-network, topology, gradient, freezing, and noise results. Existing Table 2 MNIST entries also change: residual accuracy moves from 97.52%±0.09% to 97.49%±0.05%, and AGT from 96.71%±0.14% to 96.87%±0.11%. Most existing Table 1 and Table S1 scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MLE/FTMLE definitions and first-order Taylor derivations relating EP, LRA, and BP are substantively retained in Appendices A and C.1–C.3. Renumbering and explanatory edits do not introduce new theoretical results; the added gradient-similarity evidence is empirical.

C1.justification: The main feedback-regulation, residual-connection, and speedup contributions remain. v2 removes the abstract's explicit large-scale-AI applicability assertion, changes 'fully restoring' classification performance to 'partly restoring,' and qualifies BP comparability as applying to shallow architectures.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving numerical precision, distorted random feedback, and noise accumulation. Its Discussion explicitly identifies deep/asymmetric CIFAR-10 performance gaps, untested deep-CNN applicability, empirical hyperparameter selection, and unresolved sequence-task extensions. These qualifications substantially sharpen the applicability boundaries compared with v1.

D1.justification: Appendix D expands reproducibility information with residual-network pseudocode (Algorithm S3), architecture diagrams (S14–S15), CIFAR-10 normalization, additional optimizer and scheduling settings, and default numerical precision. A new reproducibility statement describes supplementary Jupyter notebooks. The repository link and hardware descriptions were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sacramento et al., Haider et al., and Meulemans et al. to weak-feedback positioning, Veit et al. for residual-path interpretation, and Shadden et al. for finite-time Lyapunov analysis. The existing research positioning largely remains; Liu's preprint-to-publication update concerns the same cited work.

P1.justification: The original introduction–background–method–experiments–discussion progression and much prose remain. v2 polishes language, subdivides the method discussion, labels appendices A–D, improves cross-references, and adds acknowledgements and reproducibility/disclosure statements.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively retypeset from a two-column main text into a single-column ICLR layout. Tables combine testing and training values, scaling heatmaps are reorganized, and v1 Figure 5 becomes logarithmic-error Figure 6. New analytical and architecture figures are added, while retained appendix plots are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the mechanism and its practical limits. CIFAR-10 and deeper-network tests expose performance boundaries, while gradient-precision, frozen-layer, topology, and noise controls investigate credit assignment and robustness directly. More qualified performance claims and explicit limitations improve scientific calibration. These gains outweigh the loss of Fashion-MNIST coverage and training-accuracy uncertainty reporting.
